tone_statements.citation: Akinlabi, Akinbiyi & Mark Liberman. 2007. Tonal Complexes: The Prosodic Organization of Tones. Rutgers Optimality Archive ROA-911 (May 2007), 41 pp. (paper/tech report; section 5 'Tonal conspiracies in Lokaa and Tem', 5.1 'Lokaa', pp. 33-34).
tone_statements.quote: In Lokaa, an Upper Cross language of Nigeria (Faraclas 1988), verbs must have at least one high tone in isolation. A verb which has no underlyingly H tone must have one inserted. However, if there is a High tone clitic or prefix preceding the verb, H tone insertion is blocked. A less commonplace fact about Lokaa is that a noun-plus-clitic unit cannot have two high tones separated by a L tone (i.e. HLH). If cliticization creates such a sequence, it metathesizes to create a HHL sequence. ... As in the Gur languages, the domain of the tonal complex is a prosodic word. ... And like Knni, Lokaa permits the maximal tonal complex (LHL) within a tonal domain.
tone_statements.summary: Two tones, H and L (the analysis operates with H and L only; contours HL/LH arise from spreading/association, consistent with Iwara's two-toneme analysis); obligatory H per verb in isolation (default H-insertion); *HLH within the prosodic word repaired by tonal metathesis to HHL (noun+clitic, associative N1 C-H N2, relative clauses, questions); associative marker underlyingly H; maximal tonal com…

tone_statements.quote: Lokoo has two basic pitch phonemes or tonemes, which we may call high [H] and low [L] and write with acute ^ and grave v accents respectively. The following minimal pairs illustrate their phonemic contrast, and therefore their lexical function: … In addition, the language has a mid tone, which will be re­ presented by the symbol [M] in foiraulae. It has a very restricted distribution, in that it never occurs alone over a syllable, but carbines with the high or low toneme to form bitonal combinations which will be described in section 2.122.

sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2 'Lòkə́ə Phonology' (pp. 24-104) treats suprasegmentals only as tone: section 2.12 'Suprasegmental Phonemes' (p. 54-60) = two tonemes H and L (plus a mid tone restricted to bitonal combinations on long syllables), section 2.213 long-syllable tones, 2.42124/3.317 nominal tone patterns, 2.5 (p. 97ff) downdrift as the phrase-level intonation. The words 'stress'/'accent' never occur in a prosodic sense anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned layer; 'accent' only for the acute/grave diacritics). Describes the Ugep (Lòmòmò) dialect.

tone.says: Two tonemes, high and low (minimal pairs); one per short syllable, two per long syllable (H:, L:, HL, LH glides = toneme sequences); a restricted mid only in LM/HM glides of negative verbs; downdrift.
